text.title: Accessibility Evaluation Worked Example
text.summary: End-to-end example applying Accessibility Evaluation to a concrete case, plus priority-tier examples, the triage and keyboard-trace prompt patterns, and the report and scanner templates.

section.title: Triage of 3 axe findings

example.code:
## P (Perceivable) - F-001 SC 1.3.1 [critical] form#contact email input has no label. W3C H44. - F-002 SC 1.4.3 [high] body text on #hero fails 4.5:1 (3.8:1 measured). W3C G18.
## O (Operable) - F-003 SC 2.4.7 [medium] focus indicator on .card-link removed by global outline:none. W3C G149.

section.note: Each finding cites the W3C technique number; priorities differentiate sprint allocation.

example.note: Missing form label (SC 1.3.1) → Critical: screen reader users cannot identify the field; no workaround. Missing skip link (SC 2.4.1) → High: keyboard users must tab through full navigation on every page.

Triage: "Given axe-core JSON (violations[]), produce ## Detailed Findings. For each violation: WCAG SC, priority (Critical/High/Medium/Low), location (selector + page URL), recommendation (cite W3C technique G/H/F number), and minimal HTML before/after. Group by Perceivable/Operable/Understandable/Robust."

Keyboard trace: "Given Playwright keyboard-only trace, emit a row in the keyboard-testing table for: Tab navigation, Focus visible, Logical order, Skip links, Traps, Shortcuts. Pass = boolean + evidence (frame index)."
